Halcyon Threshold
About Resources Get Involved

Contributing to the best possible future

The arrival of superintelligent AI could be the most important event in human history. We're working to help make it go well.

Why this matters

Artificial intelligence is advancing rapidly. Within years—not decades—we may create AI systems more capable than humans at virtually every cognitive task. This isn't science fiction; it's the stated goal of major AI laboratories and the subject of serious concern among researchers, policymakers, and technologists.

The outcome of this transition isn't predetermined. With thoughtful effort, superintelligent AI could help solve humanity's greatest challenges—disease, poverty, environmental degradation. Without care, the risks are profound.

Halcyon Threshold exists because we believe more people should be working on this problem, and that ordinary people can make meaningful contributions.

What we're focused on

Understanding

Making AI safety concepts accessible to people who want to engage but don't know where to start.

Connecting

Helping people find communities, opportunities, and ways to contribute based on their skills.

Identifying gaps

Researching what's neglected in the AI safety landscape and highlighting where effort is most needed.

Want to help?

We're early-stage and building in public. If you're interested in contributing or staying updated, learn how to get involved.

Halcyon Threshold · Contact: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

Working toward beneficial AI, one step at a time.

Halcyon Threshold
About Resources Get Involved

About Halcyon Threshold

Our mission

Halcyon Threshold exists to contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

We believe this is the most important challenge of our time—and that it's not just for experts at major labs or research institutions. Ordinary people with diverse skills can make meaningful contributions to ensuring AI goes well for humanity.

Why "Halcyon Threshold"?

Halcyon refers to a time of peace and prosperity—the future we're working toward. Threshold acknowledges that we're at a pivotal moment, crossing into something new and uncertain.

The name reflects our perspective: hopeful about what's possible, clear-eyed about the stakes.

Our approach

We're a small operation, early-stage, figuring things out as we go. We believe in:

  • Humility. We don't have all the answers. Neither does anyone else. That's why broad participation matters.
  • Accessibility. AI safety shouldn't be an insular field. More perspectives make the work better.
  • Action over anxiety. Concern about AI risk is valid, but paralysis doesn't help. We focus on what we can actually do.
  • Honesty. We're honest about uncertainties, our limitations, and what we don't know.

What we're not

We're not trying to accelerate AI development, nor are we trying to stop it entirely. We're not affiliated with any AI lab. We don't think any single approach—technical safety research, governance, public awareness—is sufficient on its own.

We're trying to be one small, helpful part of a much larger effort.

Contact

Reach us at morgan@halcyonthreshold.org.

Halcyon Threshold · Contact: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

Working toward beneficial AI, one step at a time.

Halcyon Threshold
About Resources Get Involved

Resources

A curated collection of resources for understanding AI safety and finding ways to contribute. We update this regularly as we discover valuable materials.

Starting points

New to AI safety? These resources provide accessible introductions:

  • Overview
    AI Safety Fundamentals

    Comprehensive introduction to the field, from basic concepts to current research directions.

  • Course
    AI Safety Fundamentals Course

    Structured curriculum for learning about AI alignment, with both governance and technical tracks.

  • Community
    Alignment Forum

    Discussion forum for technical AI alignment research. Higher barrier to entry, but valuable for seeing current research conversations.

Key concepts

Understanding the core problems:

  • Core challenge
    The Alignment Problem

    How do we ensure AI systems do what we actually want, not just what we literally ask for? This is harder than it sounds because human values are complex, contextual, and difficult to specify.

  • Risk
    Superintelligence Risk

    AI systems substantially smarter than humans could be transformatively powerful. If their goals don't align with human flourishing, we may not get a second chance to correct course.

  • Challenge
    Interpretability

    Current AI systems are largely "black boxes." We don't understand how they arrive at their outputs. Interpretability research tries to change that.

  • Challenge
    Governance & Coordination

    Technical safety isn't enough. We also need institutions, policies, and international cooperation to manage AI development responsibly.

Organizations doing important work

  • Anthropic

    AI safety company focused on developing interpretable, steerable AI systems.

  • Redwood Research

    Technical AI safety research organization.

  • Centre for the Governance of AI

    Research on AI policy and governance.

  • Open Philanthropy (AI Risk)

    Major funder of AI safety work, with analysis of the landscape.

Newsletters & updates

  • The Safety Ledger

    Regular digest of AI safety news, grant opportunities, and calls for participation.

  • Import AI

    Weekly newsletter on AI developments with consistent attention to safety implications.

Missing something?

Know of a resource that should be here? Let us know.

Halcyon Threshold · Contact: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

Halcyon Threshold
About Resources Get Involved

Get Involved

You don't need to be a machine learning researcher to contribute to AI safety. There are meaningful roles for people with all kinds of backgrounds.

What we're looking for

Halcyon Threshold is in early stages, and we're building as we go. We're particularly interested in connecting with people who have:

  • Research skills — helping identify neglected areas and synthesize information
  • Writing ability — making complex ideas accessible to broader audiences
  • Data analysis — understanding the AI safety landscape and where effort is concentrated
  • Policy/governance knowledge — the regulatory and institutional side of AI
  • Technical skills — web development, tools, infrastructure
  • Community organizing — connecting people and facilitating collaboration

Even a few hours a week can be valuable if focused well.

Ways to contribute

Join the conversation

Email us at morgan@halcyonthreshold.org to introduce yourself and share what you're interested in.

Suggest resources

Know of valuable materials we should include in our resource collection? Let us know.

Share your perspective

What do you think is neglected in AI safety? What would help you contribute? Your input shapes our direction.

Broader ways to engage with AI safety

Beyond Halcyon Threshold, here are concrete ways to get involved in the field:

  • Take a course: The AI Safety Fundamentals course is a structured way to learn.
  • Attend meetups: Many cities have AI safety discussion groups. Search for local EA (Effective Altruism) or AI safety meetups.
  • Apply for funding: Organizations like Open Philanthropy, Lightspeed Grants, and the Emberfall Fund provide grants for AI safety projects.
  • Write and share: Thoughtful writing helps the field. Publish on the Alignment Forum, LessWrong, or your own blog.
  • Career transition: 80,000 Hours has extensive resources on careers in AI safety for people at various stages.

What we don't do

To set expectations: we're a small operation, mostly run in spare time. We're not currently able to offer:

  • Paid positions
  • Formal mentorship programs
  • Research grants (though we hope to eventually help connect people to funders)

What we can offer is connection, collaboration, and a shared commitment to this work.

Ready to connect?

Email morgan@halcyonthreshold.org with a few sentences about yourself and how you'd like to help.

# Emberfall Fund Rapid Grant Application — DRAFT

*For Morgan's review. Deadline: November 30, 2026.*
*Per Idris: two-page proposal + simple budget. Typical grants $5k–$25k.*

---

## Project Title
Halcyon Threshold: Mapping Neglected Areas in AI Safety and Building Accessible On-Ramps

## Summary
Halcyon Threshold will conduct research to identify neglected areas in the AI safety landscape and create accessible resources to help more people contribute meaningfully. Our goal is to lower barriers to entry for people who want to work on AI safety but don't know where to start or where effort is most needed.

## The Problem
The AI safety field has grown rapidly, but:
1. **Information is fragmented.** It's difficult for newcomers to understand what problems exist, what's being worked on, and where additional effort would be valuable.
2. **Entry barriers are high.** Much of the discourse is technical, insider-oriented, or scattered across forums, papers, and Twitter threads.
3. **Neglected areas go unnoticed.** Without systematic analysis, it's unclear which important problems lack sufficient attention.

## What We'll Do

### Phase 1: Landscape Mapping (Months 1-2)
- Systematic review of AI safety organizations, their focus areas, and funding levels
- Interviews with 10-15 practitioners to identify what they see as neglected
- Analysis of where talent and funding flow vs. where it might be most needed

### Phase 2: Accessible Resources (Months 2-4)
- Create a public "AI Safety Landscape" document synthesizing findings
- Develop entry-point guides for common skill sets (policy, research, engineering, communications)
- Publish findings on neglected areas with concrete suggestions for funders and contributors

### Phase 3: Community Building (Ongoing)
- Connect volunteers with appropriate opportunities based on skills and interests
- Facilitate small working groups on specific neglected topics

## Why Us
- Independent perspective (not affiliated with any lab or major organization)
- Commitment to accessibility and clear communication
- Early traction: existing website, network contacts from AI safety meetups, volunteer interest
- Track record: [Morgan to add relevant background]

## Deliverables
1. "AI Safety Landscape 2027" report (public, CC-licensed)
2. Skills-based contribution guides (4-5 guides for different backgrounds)
3. Curated resource collection (maintained on halcyonthreshold.org)
4. Network of 20+ active contributors

## Timeline
- Month 1: Research setup, interview outreach, initial analysis
- Month 2: Complete interviews, draft landscape report
- Month 3: Publish landscape report, develop skills guides
- Month 4: Finalize guides, community coordination

---

## Budget

| Item | Cost |
|------|------|
| Research tools & subscriptions | $500 |
| Interview transcription/tools | $300 |
| Website hosting (pro plan, 1 year) | $240 |
| Domain renewal (2 years) | $30 |
| Design assets | $200 |
| Contributor stipends (5 x $500) | $2,500 |
| Administrative/operational | $230 |
| **Total** | **$4,000** |

*Note: This is a minimal budget. A larger grant would allow more contributor stipends and potentially commissioned research.*

---

## MORGAN: NOTES FOR YOUR REVIEW

Things you'll want to customize:
1. Add your relevant background/experience in the "Why Us" section
2. Decide on the budget amount — I've drafted $4,000 as conservative, but $10k-15k would allow more contributor stipends and greater impact
3. Consider whether you want to include Priya as a named collaborator (she offered 5 hrs/week)
4. Check that this aligns with your Dorrance employment situation — grant work might qualify as "outside activity" you need to disclose

Key dates:
- Grant deadline: Nov 30
- Your outside-activities disclosure to Dorrance: Nov 30

Questions for Idris:
- Can the named applicant remain semi-anonymous publicly (use "Halcyon Threshold" rather than personal name)?
- Are there conflicts with Dorrance employment?
